summary: Wooden lookout tower on a Crawford Notch sub-peak, built about 1940; dismantled by 1968; demolished parts remain on the site.

facts.status_note: Dismantled by 1968 per the 1972 AMC guide; demolished parts of the tower remain on the site.

visit.trail_note: Leave the Nancy Pond Trail where an old fire warden's trail branches off about 1.6 miles in. The site is about 3.7 miles from the US 302 trailhead. The old trail is unmaintained.

events.note: The 1940 AMC White Mountain Guide describes a new lookout tower on the peak.
A blog estimates the tower was in operation from 1940 to 1948. The 1960 AMC guide still lists a lookout tower on the peak.
The 1972 AMC guide says the tower was dismantled in 1968.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A blog says the tower was in operation from 1940 to 1948, but the 1960 AMC guide still lists a lookout tower on the peak, and the 1972 guide gives the dismantling date as 1968. The story reports both, and records 1948 only as the blog's estimate.

sources.title: Breaking My Own Rules: A Visit to Mt. Bemis

notes_for_editor: Access is not set: no source gives an official status for the old trail. Lost Hiking Trails lists the trail as closed, possibly for safety, while the blog and SectionHiker describe a walkable, unmaintained trail. The editor should decide the access level. National Forest land is inferred from the blog's warning that removing artifacts from the National Forest is illegal; no source states the ownership outright, so the story hedges it. Agency is not set because no source names the agency that ran the tower. The NH Family Hikes list (firetowerhistory.php) files Mt. Bemis (Livermore) under 'Mountains which Once Had a Fire Tower', which agrees with the 1968 dismantling and the FFLA's gone record; it was not used as a source. An earlier version of this note said it sat under 'Other Standing Fire Towers'; that was wrong. The blog's 1961 photo date appears in a blog addendum but was not quoted, and the photo has no URL, so no photo record was added. The blog is the only source for the 1940-1948 operating span and the site description, and the state's own history was not readable (the NHDFL site returns 403). The visit trail note is drawn from blog descriptions and should be checked before publishing. The height_m value (8.8) converts the blog's 29 feet.
